newsitem.title: USA: Osram cuts jobs, moves some product lines.
newsitem.headline: Osram cuts jobs, moves some product lines.

text.p: Siemens AG unit Osram Sylvania said on Wednesday it planned to transfer several product lines from its Danvers fluorescent lamp manufacturing plant to Mexico, resulting in the loss of about 160 jobs.
The company said it would promptly schedule meetings with the union and other affected employees to discuss moves.
It said it was not sure if it would take a charge.
OSRAM said it was transfering low-speed, high-labor vertical production units to Mexico, in order to reduce the company's operating costs.

"The planned action would enable the Danvers plant to focus its resources on high-volume fluorescent lamps which account for most of the plant's current output," Richard Dolan, vice president of lamp manufacturing, said.

Vertical equipment was to be transferred to the OSRAM manufacturing plant in Mexico City where similar equipment operated. This would consolidate the company's vertical equipment technology at a single plant, OSRAM said.
